Temporal and spatial quality control in hydroTSM

Daily and sub-daily precipitation, air temperature, and streamflow

Mauricio Zambrano-Bigiarini

2026-11-10

Source: vignettes/hydroTSM_QC_temporal_spatial_tests.qmd

1 Purpose and scope

This vignette summarises the quality-control (QC) tests implemented by the frequency-aware precipQC(), tempQC(), and streamflowQC() workflows in hydroTSM. Each wrapper detects the input frequency with sfreq() and dispatches daily data to its _daily() function and minute or hourly data to its _subdaily() function. The input must be a univariate or multivariate numeric zoo object with one uniquely named station per column.

The workflows are deliberately conservative. A statistical anomaly is not automatically treated as an error: individual tests produce auditable flags, the evidence-combination stage classifies observations as review or reject, and a separate station-level decision recommends accept or discard. Every test can be activated or deactivated through the named checks argument. Spatial QC is enabled by default only when metadata is provided, although users may explicitly enable correlation-only spatial QC without coordinates.

In-memory contract

The QC functions do not write files. They return flags, suspicious-point tables, station summaries, accepted/discarded metadata, accepted zoo series, corrected accepted zoo series, spatial diagnostics when available, and all resolved settings.

In the following table, Yes means that the test is active by default, Metadata means that it defaults to active only when station metadata are supplied, Adjunct means that a separate function is available but is not called automatically, and an em dash means that the workflow does not apply that test.

3 Shared validation, metadata, and decision rules

3.1 Structural and temporal validation

All workflows reject non-numeric data, duplicated or non-increasing timestamps, empty or duplicated station names, unsupported index classes, and incompatible frequencies. Daily workflows accept Date or POSIXt indices and calculate completeness across the calendar span. Sub-daily workflows require a POSIXt index; gaps are allowed only when their duration is an integer multiple of the modal interval. The optional from and to arguments subset the in-memory record before completeness, thresholds, spatial models, and station decisions are calculated.

3.2 Station metadata and incomplete coordinates

Metadata are supplied as a data frame. Users identify the station, longitude, latitude, and optional elevation fields with station.id, coords, and elevation; streamflow may additionally identify a catchment-area field with area. Rows are matched to colnames(x), so their incoming order is irrelevant. A station is geographically located only when both longitude and latitude are finite. Missing either coordinate does not disable QC:

  • a located target applies the distance filter and prefers eligible located neighbours;
  • an unlocated target uses deterministic correlation-based candidate screening;
  • an unlocated candidate remains a conservative fallback for a located target;
  • optional elevation similarity reduces the suitability and weight of stations with very different heights; and
  • streamflow area metadata allow regressions in specific-discharge space before estimates are converted back to the target station’s units.

3.3 Spatial scalability

Spatial tests use compact target-specific candidate lists rather than dense station-by-station distance matrices. max.candidates=200L bounds the pool retained for exact selection, and selection.samples=2048L bounds the deterministic, evenly spaced time sample used for initial neighbour screening. Final estimates and flags always use the full record. Setting either control to Inf requests the corresponding exhaustive behaviour. Work can be distributed with ncores, parallel.type ("serial", "socket", or "fork"), and optional cluster.nodes.

3.4 Evidence and station recommendations

The workflows distinguish hard tests from tests that normally require corroboration:

  • precipitation daily treats range, copied blocks, clustered frequent values, distribution gaps, persistence, misplaced accumulation, and spatially corroborated dry spells as hard evidence; sub-daily precipitation treats range, persistence, daily/monthly accumulation, and dry spells as hard;
  • temperature daily treats range, copied blocks, persistence, and spikes as hard; sub-daily temperature treats range, persistence, and spikes as hard;
  • streamflow daily treats range and copied blocks as hard, while sub-daily streamflow treats only range as hard because real operations and flashy catchments can resemble statistical errors.

Non-hard flags are confirmed when at least min.evidence independent test families agree. Station recommendations additionally use missing, review, confirmed-suspicious, record-duration, and optional breakpoint criteria. The default correction is "none"; "set_na" removes confirmed points, and "spatial" substitutes an available spatial estimate and otherwise uses NA.

4 Precipitation QC

The precipitation design combines gross-error, temporal, climatological, and neighbour-consistency checks used in operational rain-gauge QC (Hamada et al. 2011; Scherrer et al. 2011; Lewis et al. 2021; El Hachem et al. 2022).

4.1 Daily precipitation

Check key and function Default behaviour What is flagged
range — precipQC_range() lower=0, upper=1825 mm d(^{-1}) Negative values or values above the configured physical limit. The upper default is a conservative 24-hour record screen, not a regional design threshold.
duplicate — precipQC_duplicate() At least 20 paired month positions or 300 paired year positions, with at least three wet values Entire calendar months or years copied exactly at corresponding positions (Durre et al. 2010).
frequency — precipQC_frequency() Consecutive wet reports with 9/10, 8/10, 7/10, or 5/10 identical values, screened by 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, or 0.9 climatological probabilities Suspicious clustering caused by rounding, coding, or repeated manual entries (Durre et al. 2010).
gap — precipQC_gap() A gap of at least 300 mm in a calendar-month wet-value distribution Values in the separated upper tail above the first large distribution gap (Durre et al. 2010).
climatology — precipQC_climatology() 15-day circular day-of-year window; probability 0.999; robust score 8; at least 30 samples Upper extremes beyond both an empirical quantile and a robust iterative log1p median/MAD limit.
persistence — precipQC_persistence() Five identical consecutive values of at least 10 mm d(^{-1}) Repeated high values consistent with stuck, copied, or artificial reports.
accumulation — precipQC_accumulation() Candidate exceeds twice the station mean wet-day depth and follows a missing previous day A multi-day amount plausibly assigned to one daily timestamp. It is a candidate flag, not proof of accumulation.
weekday — precipQC_weekday() At least 20 wet days in a station-year; chi-squared alpha=0.001; observed/expected ratio at most 0.5 Dry reports on a strongly under-recorded weekday, targeting systematic false zeros in manually observed networks (Estevez et al. 2022).
breakpoint — precipQC_breakpoint() Pettitt tests on annual total, wet-day count, maximum, and extreme-day count; Holm adjustment A station-level homogeneity change. It is diagnostic and does not discard a station unless discard.breakpoint=TRUE (Stepanek et al. 2009).

The daily spatial test is applied to rolling 1-, 3-, and 7-day totals by default. One native-scale neighbour graph is selected with Spearman correspondence on log1p precipitation and reused at every scale. For each target and time, precipQC_spatial() calculates an ordinary or distance/elevation-weighted neighbour median. The critical ratio divides the positive transformed residual by the larger of simultaneous neighbour dispersion, historical residual dispersion, and a numerical floor. An accumulation endpoint flag is expanded to all contributing daily values. Multi-scale testing prevents an error hidden at one accumulation from being missed at another (El Hachem et al. 2022).

precipQC_dryspell() separately examines default 15-day target dry windows. A window is flagged when the requested neighbour fraction (default 1) records at least three wet days. This targets false zeros or missing rainfall that an upper-outlier test cannot detect (Lewis et al. 2021; Golkhatmi and Farzandi 2024).

4.2 Sub-daily precipitation

Check key Default behaviour and difference from daily QC
range The upper limit is max.rate=401 mm h(^{-1}) multiplied by the detected interval duration; negative depths are invalid (Lewis et al. 2021).
climatology Month-specific log1p limits use probability 0.999, robust score 8, and at least 100 observations.
persistence Two identical high values are suspicious. When no high threshold is supplied, it is twice the station mean wet-day depth. Any identical wet value persisting for 24 hours is also flagged.
daily.accumulation A large interval is screened against 23 dry hours before and after it.
monthly.accumulation A large interval is screened against 28 preceding dry days and 23 following dry hours.
weekday Native values are first aggregated to daily totals only when at least 90% of expected intervals are present; daily weekday flags are expanded back to finite dry native intervals.
breakpoint Native precipitation is aggregated to daily totals before the annual multi-indicator Pettitt analysis.

Spatial consistency is evaluated at the native interval and 1, 3, 6, and 24 hours by default. Positive durations must be exact multiples of the detected interval. Accumulated flags are expanded back to their contributing native observations. The same 15-day dry-spell logic is applied after in-memory daily wet/dry aggregation. Raw tipping-bucket inter-tip checks cannot be reconstructed from already accumulated zoo values; they require the original tip timestamps (Villalobos-Herrera et al. 2022).

5 Air-temperature QC

Temperature QC combines physical limits, robust seasonal references, temporal consistency, spatial regression, and homogeneity diagnostics (Durre et al. 2010; Feng et al. 2004; Hubbard et al. 2007; Brunet et al. 2020).

5.1 Daily air temperature

Check key and function Default behaviour What is flagged
range — tempQC_range() (-89.4) to (57.7) degrees C Values outside global physical screening limits. Regional limits should be supplied when authoritative.
duplicate — tempQC_duplicate() At least 20 paired month or 300 paired year positions Exactly copied complete months or years (Durre et al. 2010).
climatology — tempQC_climatology() Circular 15-day day-of-year window; robust absolute score 6; at least 100 samples Values far from the local seasonal median relative to MAD/IQR dispersion (Feng et al. 2004; Durre et al. 2010).
persistence — tempQC_persistence() Seven observations with range no greater than zero Exact flat lines consistent with a stuck sensor. persistence.tolerance can admit near-flat lines.
step — tempQC_step() Month-specific first differences; robust score 3; at least 20 differences Implausible consecutive-day changes; optional absolute rise/fall limits may also be imposed (Hubbard et al. 2007).
spike — tempQC_spike() Centre value at least 25 degrees from both neighbours in the same direction An isolated spike or dip (Durre et al. 2010).
breakpoint — tempQC_breakpoint() Pettitt tests on sufficiently complete annual means and standard deviations; at least 10 years; Holm-adjusted alpha=0.05; shift at least 1 degree A station-level homogeneity change, diagnostic by default (Boulanger et al. 2010; Brunet et al. 2020).

tempQC_spatial() selects up to five neighbours using overall Pearson correlation and proximity-adjusted target-on-neighbour regression error. It fits separate monthly regressions, combines their predictions with geographic/elevation proximity and inverse-error-variance weights, and flags a target only when both the absolute residual (default 8 degrees) and the standardised residual (default 4) are large. Pairwise intercepts estimate persistent station offsets without imposing a universal lapse rate. This is a resistant spatial-regression-test implementation for complex terrain (Hubbard et al. 2007; Estevez et al. 2018; Xiong et al. 2022, 2024).

5.2 Sub-daily air temperature

Check key Default behaviour and difference from daily QC
range Uses the same configurable physical limits as daily temperature.
climatology References are conditioned jointly on calendar month and hour; the robust score is 6 with at least 30 samples.
persistence A range no greater than 0.05 degrees across a default three-hour duration is flagged; the observation count is derived from the detected interval (Beele et al. 2022).
step Month-hour first differences use robust score 5 and at least 30 samples.
spike The isolated spike/dip threshold is 12 degrees.
spatial Regressions are fitted separately by month and hour, with minimum absolute residual 5 degrees, standardised residual 4, and preferred correlation at least 0.7 (Cheng et al. 2016).
breakpoint Native observations are aggregated to daily means before annual homogeneity analysis.

When paired Tmin and Tmax series are available, the adjunct tempQC_internal() flags Tmin greater than Tmax, possible interchange relative to the previous/current/following-day window, and excessive lagged separation. This test is intentionally separate because a single generic temperature matrix cannot reveal which member of an inconsistent Tmin/Tmax pair is wrong.

6 Streamflow QC

Streamflow QC is cautious about hydrologically real extremes, intermittent zeros, regulation, tidal behaviour, and rapidly responding catchments. It therefore keeps physical impossibilities separate from statistical evidence and combines correlated high-flow diagnostics into one evidence family (Gudmundsson et al. 2018; Crochemore et al. 2020; U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System 2018).

6.1 Daily streamflow

Check key and function Default behaviour What is flagged
range — streamflowQC_range() lower=0, upper=Inf Negative/non-finite non-missing discharge and optional station-specific upper-limit violations.
duplicate — streamflowQC_duplicate() At least 20 paired month or 300 paired year positions and one positive value Exactly copied calendar blocks; all-zero intermittent-flow blocks are protected by default.
gap — streamflowQC_gap() Expected interval one day The first finite observation after a missing value or missing calendar interval.
climatology — streamflowQC_climatology() log(Q + 0.01); circular five-day window; mean plus/minus six standard deviations; at least 30 samples Seasonally implausible low or high flow following the GSIM structure (Gudmundsson et al. 2018).
flatline — streamflowQC_flatline() More than 10 equal positive daily values (run=11); zeros protected Extended constant or near-constant flow.
spike — streamflowQC_spike() Factor-five reversal or change larger than the station 0.99 quantile An isolated peak or dip.
rate — streamflowQC_rate() Monthly robust log-difference score 6, optional absolute limits, and factor-five abrupt fall Implausible consecutive changes.
highflow — streamflowQC_highflow() Global log-flow score 6; largest/second-largest AMAX ratio 2; GEV return period 1000 years after at least 10 annual maxima Exceptionally high flows. Component flags and return-period diagnostics are retained, but they count as one evidence family.
breakpoint — streamflowQC_breakpoint() Pettitt tests on annual mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum; at least 10 years; Holm alpha=0.01; relative change at least 0.5 A station-level change that may indicate measurement change, regulation, or catchment change.

The daily spatial test selects up to five neighbours using Spearman correlation on log flow plus optional distance/elevation proximity. With area metadata, target-on-neighbour models operate on specific discharge. A target event must exceed its 0.99 quantile, have a spatial residual score of at least 3, and lack the required neighbour support (default one neighbour above its 0.95 quantile) within three days before or after the event. Thus a genuine regional flood is corroborated rather than rejected solely because it is extreme.

6.2 Sub-daily streamflow

Check key Default behaviour and difference from daily QC
range Uses the same non-negative physical rule and optional upper limit.
gap The expected interval is the detected modal interval in seconds.
climatology Month-specific log(Q + 0.01) limits use score 6 and at least 100 observations.
flatline Ordinary flat lines use 168 hours; high-flow flat lines above the 0.99 quantile use 24 hours. Durations are converted to observation counts.
spike Uses the same factor-five/0.99-quantile isolated-reversal logic.
rate Monthly log-difference score 6, optional absolute limits, and factor-five abrupt fall.
fluctuation — streamflowQC_fluctuation() More than eight derivative sign reversals in 16 observations after suppressing changes below the 0.05 absolute-difference quantile
highflow Native values feed the same log-flow, AMAX-ratio, and GEV diagnostics.
breakpoint Native values are aggregated to daily means before annual Pettitt tests.

Sub-daily spatial event support uses a default 72-hour window rather than a fixed observation count. The target and neighbour quantiles, regression score, specific-discharge option, and conservative lack-of-support rule otherwise match the daily formulation. These rules generalise operational sub-daily flow QC to the actual modal interval (Fileni et al. 2023; Zhao et al. 2018).

7 Activating and deactivating tests

Names omitted from checks retain their workflow defaults. This allows a small override rather than restating the complete vector:

# Keep daily precipitation defaults but disable weekday and breakpoint tests.
p.qc <- precipQC_daily(
  p, metadata=stations,
  checks=c(weekday=FALSE, breakpoint=FALSE)
)

# Explicitly enable correlation-only spatial temperature QC without metadata.
t.qc <- tempQC_subdaily(
  temperature,
  checks=c(spatial=TRUE),
  ncores=4, parallel.type="socket"
)

# Retain streamflow temporal tests but disable high-flow and spatial evidence.
q.qc <- streamflowQC(
  discharge,
  checks=c(highflow=FALSE, spatial=FALSE)
)

Thresholds should be adapted when authoritative regional limits, instrument resolution, catchment behaviour, or network operating practices are known. The defaults are screening values grounded in the cited literature; they are not universal proof that an observation is wrong.

8 Returned audit trail

The three result classes share a common audit structure:

  • accepted.metadata and discarded.metadata preserve user metadata;
  • accepted.data contains accepted station series without modification;
  • corrected.data applies the requested correction only to accepted stations;
  • flags retains every enabled point-level test separately;
  • suspicious lists station, timestamp, value, contributing tests, evidence, and action;
  • station.summary records completeness, review/rejection fractions, record length, breakpoint evidence, and recommendation;
  • spatial estimates, scores, neighbours, and streamflow event-support counts remain available when spatial QC ran; and
  • settings records the resolved thresholds, subset bounds, and parallel backend for reproducibility.

Plots from plot.precipQC(), plot.tempQC(), and plot.streamflowQC() summarise station recommendations, the most affected stations, flags by test, and the timing of confirmed suspicious observations.

9 Limitations

These workflows evaluate the zoo observations and metadata supplied to them. They cannot reconstruct logger diagnostics, raw tipping-bucket tip times, rating-curve revisions, maintenance logs, observer notes, or upstream operations that are absent from those inputs. Spatial agreement is also not independence: common radar adjustments, shared telemetry, regional storms, or basin-wide regulation can affect several stations together. Final rejection and correction decisions should therefore retain the audit trail and, for high-impact records, include expert review.
